findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand washing sink in the infant room to contain a paintbrush in the sink basin. CORRECTED- the paint brush was removed from the sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for hand washing only. A blocked sink/ a sink used for other purposes may deter frequent hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ambient thermometer to be missing from the refrigerator in the infant room. CORRECTED- an ambient thermometer was placed in the door. Ensure all cold holding units contain an ambient thermometer placed in the warmest part of the unit to ensure temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are held at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: Inspector observed handle of serving utensil in the oranges. Gloves are worn when serving but still food must be protected from the handle. The serving time was at the end. Breakfast is from 8:30am to 10am. The few oranges remaining were discarded. The kitchen staff was reminded of the rule. They said that they usually use a smaller bowl and the handle does not usually does not come into contact with the food. 

FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

Mouse droppings are present on the counter behind the microwave and on the window sill. The facility has cleaned and sanitized the area. Maintain the area free of droppings. The facility caught a mouse on Monday, 10/9/23.  The inspector will be back to follow up on 10/23/23.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Mouse soil observed on the counter behind the microwave and the window sill. The area was cleaned and sanitized at time of inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

Mice droppings still present on bottom dry storage shelves and behind fridge. Clean and sanitized. Inspector will follow-up on 4/22/22.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Facility will be followed up on next week;. Mouse problem is noted throughout the facility Sentinel is coming on Monday 4/18.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. The coving in the employee bathroom is coming away from the wall - re-seal.
2. Caulk is needed at the hand sinks near the kitchen. No caulk was observed between the sink and wall.

Ensure repairs before next routine inspection. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/8/21.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements - out of compliance. Reviewed document with PIC's. Discussed importance and need for all food handler's to sign - retain documents in public health folder. Provided paperwork for requirements for diagnosed food service employees and requirements for symptomatic employees for reporting, exclusion, and restriction. Reviewed documents. Paperwork was noted as given during last routine inspection - 3/11/19. Inspector will follow-up on 04/19/21.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

Observed open beverage can in the kitchen. Beverages should have a closed lid. Discussed practice with PIC and food handler. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

(REPEAT) Observed no hand washing between tasks by the food handler. In between tasks, hands should be washed in a hank sink with soap, hot water, and paper towels. A barrier to turn off the faucet should be used such as the paper towel. Discussion was held with PIC's and the food handler. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/11/19.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed basket of single-use spoons to not be prewrapped or stored in a manner that allows handles being touched by employees inappropriately. Handles are stored in both directions allowing access to touch food- and lip-contact surfaces - cross contamination. Cease practice. Store single-use utensils in a manner that allows access to only handles without touching food- and lip-contact surfaces when retrieving items.

Observed pots and cooking utensils in the stove area to be stored in a manner that allows access to cross contamination - invert pots and cooking utensils on top shelf. 

Discussed practices with PIC's.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. The shelving boards that are storing the pots and cooking utensils within the stove area need repainted.
2. The shelf by the 3 compartment sink is in need of being repainted.
3. The coving in the employee bathroom is coming away from the wall - re seal
4. Caulk is needed at the hand sinks near the kitchen. No caulk was observed between the sink and wall. 

Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-202.11: Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas. 

Observed no light shield for lighting within the stove area. Discussed purchasing light shield with PIC's.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Person in charge of food prep/service has a food handler certification but does not have a manager certification. Owner and director have manager certifications but were informed the person in charge of food service needs to be a certified food manager as well. Information was provided for food sanitation courses. 

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook went between tasks and was not observed washing hands at any point during the inspection. Food was in the process of being prepared for lunch, dishes were being washed, and various surfaces were touched. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. 

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after leaving the kitchen and upon returning prior to handling anything related to food service and after handling soiled dishes/equipment.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114  Concentration of bleach solution in ware washing sink was observed at 50ppm. Concentration required per label instructions shows an effective concentration of 100-200ppm. Can opener was sanitized in the solution based on information provided. Cook was advised to re-sanitize the can opener prior to next use and maintain sanitizing solution for ware washing at proper concentration as directed per manufacturer instructions. Solution was emptied to be remade after lunch service. 

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 150-200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Stem of the food thermometer was observed to be soiled with stuck on food debris. Stem was wiped with inspector's alcohol wipe. Proper use and care of stem thermometers was discussed. 

Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes are used during prep, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Chili that was cooked in advance for lunch another day this week was observed in the fridge. Stock pot was placed in the fridge to cool after it was cooked around 7a based on information provided by the cook. Chili had a surface and internal temperatures of 75°F and 82°F respectively. Owner chose to discard the chili and will prepare chili fresh for same day service later this week. Proper cooling was discussed, and educational handouts were provided.  (See general comments for additional information)

Cooked time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135ºF to 70°F and within an additional 4 hours from 70°F to 41°F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135ºF to 41°F/below.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11 Chemical bottles in one cabinet under the ware washing sinks were observed without labels. Bottles were emptied during the inspection. Proper labeling of chemical spray bottles was discussed. 

Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site (bleach solution) shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Raid insecticide was observed in one of the cabinets with cleaning supplies under the ware washing sinks. Owner discarded the product during inspection. Proper storage and use of toxics were discussed. Owner was advised to work with a pest control company to determine a proper option for insecticide use in the facility. 

Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state use is allowed in a food establishment.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometers were checked for accuracy with an ice water solution. One stem thermometer was reading at 25°F while the other was around 33°F. The thermometer observed at 25°F was calibrated to 32°F in the ice water solution. Calibration was discussed, and educational handout was provided. 

Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the can opener blade to be soiled during the inspection. Wash, rinse and sanitize the can opener blade as needed. The blade was pulled during the inspection and cleaned.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed eggs above ready to eat foods stored in the refrigerator. Make sure to store foods in the proper way to prevent from potential cross contamination.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
Upon the arrival of the inspection, the inspector observed an employee making turkey and cheese sandwiches with no gloves. Use minimal bare hand contact when touching ready to eat foods.
750-160 Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the can opener blade soiled. The can opener was pulled during the inspection.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed raw hamburger stored above tortellini. Ensure proper storage in all cold holding units. Items were moved during the inspection.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the sanitizer bottle used to wipe childrens' tables and food contact surfaces is measuring 10ppm. The sanitizer was remade during the inspection and measuring 100ppm. Test the sanitizer before each use to make sure it is the proper concentration.
750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed 3 house flies and 10+ fruit flies in the establishment. Provide proper pest control measures.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed ground chuck stored improperly in the reach in freezer. Store the ground chuck in a manner to prevent potential cross contamination.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Observed no chlorine test kit for the facility. Provide a chlorine test kit.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Ovserved a stack of cups on top  of the refrigeration unit shich is coated with dust  750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents . contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Bottom 3 cups were discarded, clean cups placed back in sleeve in box  and the top of fridge will be cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Shelves holding spices and dry goods along with shelves in coolers have some accumulated soil.  750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: The wall behind clean utensil drying area has chipped paint. The ceiling above the oven in the closet has a fan cover that is soiled and in disrepair. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings. Seal wall behind dish drainers. Replace fan vent cover with one that is of a material which is durable under conditions of normal use. (most likely metal)

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Employee spoons stored in a white plastic container in the drawer which has crumbs in the bottom. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Bin was placed into wash side of sink.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: All freezers need wiped out in the bottoms. There are accumulated crumbs. Also some drawers in the kitchen area have dust. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain areas free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: An open glass of water is on the table where sandwiches are being made. 750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food. Use only clean covered containers with a lid and straw for personal beverage storage. Store them away from food prep areas.  Glass was removed.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Box of pan liners is on the floor in the oven closet. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law. Move box of single use items up so that it is properly protected.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: Bag of small pet bedding is stored in the oven closet. 750-1350c Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items. Bedding was removed.  Keep food areas reserved for food related items only.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Sanitizer concentration in the three part sink was less than 50ppm approximately 10 ppm. 750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration. Two cap measures of bleach were added to the sink and the concentration reached 50ppm.  The concentration of sanitizer can be affected by different variables and therefore should be tested each time the sink is remade and at regular intervals.
